Stated Claim / Post Context:
White House AI Task Force Adopts Charter, Starts 120-Day Clock

The White House’s artificial intelligence task force adopted its charter Thursday, opening a 120-day window to advise on how much of an oversight role Washington should take.
The post White House AI Task Force Adopts Charter, Starts 120-Day Clock appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
The White House’s artificial intelligence task force adopted its charter Thursday, opening a 120-day window to advise on how much of an oversight role Washington should take.

The panel agreed after its first official meeting to commission a report from the President’s Council of Advisers on Science and Technology evaluating AI risk, according to Semafor. The review covers cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure protection, biosecurity and dual-use applications, and model control and accountability.

A White House official said the group would reach outside government as it carries out its mandate.

Throughout its work, the [task force] will engage with frontier model developers and other SI companies, consumer protection groups, and civil liberties advocates, industry stakeholders, and federal and state law enforcement agencies to inform and implement its efforts.

The task force also created a working group to implement the White House Accord on Super Intelligence that major AI chief executives signed this month, a process led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, the task force’s chair, alongside National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.

Defense Undersecretary Emil Michael, a vice chair, will develop protocols for labs to report breaches, hacks, and other cyber incidents to the government. The Pentagon official will also interface with frontier labs on long-term coordination across the government.

FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson will lead a law-enforcement and consumer-protection committee that includes the Justice Department, while Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor will handle critical-infrastructure protection and study AI’s impact on the American workforce with the Labor Department.

Members include Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, along with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and her deputy, Richard Walters.

A White House official told Semafor that one potential lever is export controls, which the Commerce Department temporarily imposed on Anthropic after the company declined to grant the government unfettered access to its models.

The task force’s work follows President Donald Trump’s September 29 executive order directing federal agencies to replace “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence,” signed the same day roughly two dozen technology executives attended a White House luncheon and six frontier firms signed the voluntary Accord that Trump called “morally binding.”

Clayton, a former SEC chairman confirmed as intelligence chief over the summer, told the Wall Street Journal the administration’s priority is keeping the United States ahead of China.

“The risk of not being first is high,” Clayton said.

‘Kinky’ NY Dem House candidate doubles down on explicit bondage ads

“I make Christian Grey look like amateur hour,” Gallant quipped to the Times, referencing the erotic billionaire entrepreneur in the bondage romance book and film series “50 Shades of Grey.”

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Long Island Democratic congressional hopeful has made it clear in a recent interview that he is not ashamed of his past bondage modeling photos uncovered by The Post last month.

Chris Gallant, 37, the Democratic nominee running against Rep. Nick LaLota (R-NY) in the NY-01 district says he chose to pose for the racy photos almost 17 years ago because he was into it — not because he was manipulated — and he bragged that he thought he looked great, he told The New York Times.

“I mean, all my friends know I’m kinky” as hell, he told the newspaper — “except he used a much saltier word than ‘hell,’” the Times noted.

“I make Christian Grey look like amateur hour,” he quipped to the outlet, referencing the erotic billionaire entrepreneur in the bondage romance book and film series “50 Shades of Grey.”

In an explosive report last month, The Post uncovered Gallant posed for photos for “Mr. S Leather,” a San Francisco-based purveyor of leather-daddy supplies, modelling collars, leather straps and bondage gear among other things.

Other images of Gallant in Mr. S Leather gear appear to have shown up on gay porn sites that do not appear to be affiliated with “Mr. S Leather.”

The congressional hopeful’s Los Angeles and New York-based attorney Sara Azari told The Post in September that Gallant’s limited understanding with “Mr. S Leather” was “never intended to authorize unrestricted publication” by third parties.

The images of Gallant are no longer featured on the stores’ site but are still accessible in internet archives, which show they were online between 2011 and 2020.

“The photographs are authentic and were taken during a private, consensual photo session involving Chris and his then-partner, with whom he was in a committed four-year relationship,” Azari noted.

“Chris was also friends with the owner of Mr. S Leather, and the shoot was intended to be fun and personal, with the understanding that Mr. S could use select images in connection with certain products,” she said, adding the pictures “have no bearing on Chris’s record, qualifications, judgment, or ability to serve.”

Azari noted: “As Chris began considering a future in public service, he asked that the photographs no longer be used and that they be removed from the company’s website. Mr. S honored his request.”

“I just thought, ‘If my family can accept me, the world can,’ and that’s how I lived my entire life,” he told the Times for the new article.

After The Post’s report, Gallant’s campaign then launched a social ad which read: “Make Politics Sexy Again” and joked to the Times that maybe this could be his “Kim Kardashian moment.”

But he told the publication he didn’t expect his old bondage photos would have become as public as they did. “I mean, you had to go hunt for this,” he explained to the Times.

He addressed the photos directly in a social media post after the bombshell report, labeling it as “a coordinated political hit meant to drive me out of this race” and noting “I am very proud of who I am.”

Gallant told the Times the “most difficult thing was always getting my name out there or trying to improve that.”

“And there’s definitely been a name-recognition increase on the world stage,” Gallant told the publication, noting that “The Daily Show” covered his modeling photos.

Host Michael Kosta joked on the late-night program: “New York, baby, where Democrat Chris Gallant is running to represent New York’s first congressional district, and he’s getting his ass beaten, but not in the polls.”

Gallant, a Black Hawk helicopter pilot, has served in the Army National Guard since 2006, according to his LinkedIn profile — likely during the time he posed for the kinky images.

The Long Island-raised nominee also serves as a volunteer firefighter and previously worked as a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) air traffic controller, where he had been a local union chapter leader in the National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA).

The Post reached out to Gallant’s campaign for comment.
